_comment: THE INTENSIFICATION LADDER (docs/plan_intensification_ladder.md §5). Both food webs climb the same ladder: rung 1 = the wild source, rung 2 = you manage it in place, rung 3 = you control its reproduction. A rung is a RECORD; the ladder is a LIST; adding a rung is appending a record. THIS FILE DESCRIBES WHAT THE SIM DOES TODAY, not the target model — later slices change behaviour by EDITING it (that is the whole thesis). A rung whose `verb` is null is not driven by a policy today and the build engine skips it.
_comment_branches: `plant` = the human food web (forage patches, forage.rs). `animal` = the animal food web (herds, fauna.rs). The two learn separately (§4.2) and never share a rung.
_comment_build: `build` is the PER-SOURCE meter the rung's verb fills, and IT IS PRICED IN WORK, NOT IN TURNS (docs/plan_unit_costed_work.md). `work_cost` = the fixed size of the job in WORK UNITS, where ONE UNIT IS ONE WORKER-TURN AT THE FOOD PEAK WITH NO GEAR (intensification::PER_WORKER_OUTPUT = 1.0, deliberately NOT a config dial — the cost side is the one authority over pacing). So a crew of n BARE-HANDED workers produces n units a turn, and the kit it brought raises what each of them delivers; TURNS ARE THE OUTPUT, so the same fixed job finishes sooner as the faction puts more hands, a shallower floor or better tools on it. THE BUILD IS RAISED BY THE BAND'S BUILDERS POOL (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.5): a verb DECLARES and names no crew — cultivate/sow/tame/corral <faction> <target...> and extend_pen append an entry to that band's ORDERED BUILD QUEUE — and the hands stand on `assign_labor <faction> <band> builders <n>`, whose WHOLE output goes on the head of the queue until that entry's meter fills, then on the next. The take crew on the source and the two keeping pools (agriculture/husbandry) are separate rows drawing on the same finite band, so competing for hands IS the opportunity cost and it is visible in the numbers the player typed. THERE IS NO CAP ON ANY ROLE: fifty builders finish a Cultivate in a turn, and that is allowed. THE BUILD RATE NO LONGER READS THE FLOOR: `a crew pulling hard on the source it is improving builds slowly` was written when ONE crew did both jobs, and a build crew on a source nobody is harvesting has no floor to read at all. learn_multiplier stays on the KNOWLEDGE accrual, where how much you leave standing still shapes what you learn. Pacing is unchanged at the default floor, where that multiplier was exactly 1.0. RETIRED: `decay_fraction_per_turn`, the fraction of a rung's own cost bled on a turn nobody worked it. SHORTFALL IS THE DECAY (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.4): what an improvement loses is EXACTLY the work nobody supplied toward its `upkeep`, so a second dial saying how fast it forgets is a second answer to a question the upkeep already answers — and the two could disagree, giving a rung that bleeds faster than it costs to hold. `grace_turns` = how many consecutive UNWORKED turns the rung forgives before its neglect penalty starts, and it is now THE ANIMAL BRANCH'S ALONE (animals shed animals over their labor capacity). NULL on both plant rungs: a plant rung's penalty is its upkeep shortfall, so its grace is `upkeep.grace_turns` and a second number here would be a dial nothing reads. THE CREW'S TOOLS RAISE THE WORKER, AND A JOB'S WORK REQUIREMENT NEVER CHANGES (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.8): each equipped worker delivers PER_WORKER_OUTPUT + EquipmentStat::build_work per turn, resolved through the partly-equipped-party coverage seam, and the meter completes at work_cost - the same work_cost bare-handed and fully equipped. RETIRED: the effective bar, work_cost - (workers x build_work), which took the crew's tools off the JOB. It granted the kit's help as a LUMP against the target, once, however long the job ran, where a tool is used every turn it is held; and it has nothing to subtract from on an `upkeep`, which is a rate rather than a pile, so one supply expression now feeds both accounts - a build divides a pile by it, an upkeep compares a demand against it. What that gives up is scale-sensitivity: a multiple on the crew cancels the cost, so it saves the same PERCENTAGE of turns on a garden and a farm alike, where a lump off the cost was a larger share of a small job. Accepted. RETIRED: `crew_needed`, a per-rung staffing FLOOR on the source's published workers_needed. It existed because a source's worker cap was inverted out of its TAKE, and a crew building paid a dipped take, so committing to a 25-turn Cultivate made the panel ask for ONE forager where the same wild patch asks for two. THE PLAYER STAFFS EACH ROLE NOW (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.5): there is no blended head count for a floor to raise, and workers_needed is answered PER ROLE from the work model. RETIRED: `yield_fraction_while_building`, the investment dip, 0.50 on all four rungs that declared a build. It said 'this crew is preparing ground, not gathering' — A WORK-BUDGET CONFLICT HARDCODED AS A FRACTION (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.2). SEPARATE ROWS make it arithmetic instead: the gatherers on a source take exactly what their hands carry whatever is being built beside them, and what a build costs is the people standing on the `builders` role instead of on the range. The split falls out of the HEAD COUNTS the player stated rather than out of a dial, so wanting both means assigning more hands. (The interim `WorkBudget` — one crew-turn as one pool, upkeep drawing first — is retired too: the dip and a work budget cannot both be live without double-counting.) Four magic numbers went with it, along with a term nobody chose (the plant rungs sat at 0.25 for years purely because that was the pre-move `cultivating_yield_fraction`). Null on a rung with no build (the wild rungs — there is nothing to build about a wild source).
_comment_upkeep: `upkeep` is WHAT IT COSTS TO HOLD THE RUNG, PER TURN, FOREVER (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2) — the RATE half of the ladder beside `build`'s PILE, in the SAME work units, so 'what does it cost to hold this' has one answer in one unit whichever rung is asked. THERE ARE THREE DIALS AND THEY ANSWER THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. (1) `work_per_turn` = THE DEMAND, how much work a turn holding this wants, before the scale term. `scaled_by` = a bounded coded primitive (the `behavior` idiom), and `source_load` is the ONLY VARIANT TODAY: x the source's own load reading, in whatever unit that web measures itself in — keeper-loads on the animal web (head count / animals_per_herder, fauna_config.json) and TENDER-LOADS on the plant web (the TILE's own K / labor_config.json's forage.cultivation.capacity_per_tender). The shape is the pen's on both: twice the load, twice the keeping. The retired variant was `flat`, the rate as declared; the two plant rungs carried it on the reading that a patch is one tile so nothing could ride the rate, and a tile's own K turned out to be exactly that count. THE ROUTE BRANCH READS IT TOO, and that is what tested the per-branch idea: a road's load is its own tile's infrastructure_cost times its remoteness from the band that keeps it. `RouteSpan` was added for a road's `length x terrain` and COLLAPSED back into this variant when a road became a per-tile improvement (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13b) - per tile there is no length term, so both arms were one expression and the second variant was a second name for one measure. The `scaled_by` key stays in config so the rung-monotonicity check keeps meaning something. (2) `meter_decay` = THE RATE IT ROTS AT once you fall short: `per_turn` is what a WHOLLY unmaintained rung loses off its meter every turn, and the loss is PROPORTIONAL — decay = (shortfall / demand) x per_turn — so half the hands means half the rot. (3) `grace_turns` = HOW LONG under-supplied before any of it starts, consecutive turns forgiven, its own number because a rung may be forgiving about an unworked build and strict about an unpaid bill. THE DECAY USED TO BE THE SHORTFALL ITSELF, which welded (1) to (2): raising a demand made the improvement rot faster in exact proportion, so neither number could be retuned. Splitting them is what let the plant demands move to whole numbers (2 and 4) while the rot rate stayed exactly where it was (0.5 and 0.75) — provably pacing-neutral on the decay axis. `meter_decay.retain_fraction` IS DELETED, NOT RETUNED (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.8/4.10). It was a stamped bar BELOW a rung's own cost at which the rung was revoked, and it existed because a completed meter sits EXACTLY at its cost, so the first bleed of any size took the rung away. THE ONE-POSITION LADDER REMOVES THE CLIFF IT PATCHED: a source has ONE POSITION in cumulative work units and every rung's payout INTERPOLATES on it, so a patch at 49.99 of the tended rung's 50 pays 99.98% of a tended patch. The predicate flipping there is no longer a value cliff — it only changes which job the next-rung offer names. A rung is achieved at position >= its top and lost the instant it dips. DO NOT RE-ADD A BAR WITHOUT FIRST RE-ADDING THE CLIFF. `meter_decay` IS NULL ON BOTH ANIMAL RUNGS and that is not an omission: an under-kept flock SHEDS ANIMALS at fauna_config's own pen_escape_fraction / pastoral_escape_fraction, which are already the rate — a second one here would be two numbers for one mechanic, free to disagree. Only the shortfall FRACTION is shared. WHICH HANDS ANSWER DEPENDS ON WHETHER THE RUNG IS BUILT: a meter still being RAISED is owed its BUILDERS, one being HELD is owed the band's MAINTENANCE POOL. You cannot be billed to hold something you have not finished building (section 0), so a Cultivate runs at its stated pace with no keeper at all; an ABANDONED part-build still bleeds, because the hands it needed are not on it either. MAINTENANCE IS A BAND-LEVEL STANDING ROLE NOW (`agriculture` for the plant web, `husbandry` for the animal one), not a per-source crew: the band's demand is the SUM over everything it holds on that web and the pool supplies against that total, so nothing is wasted on a demand that does not divide into whole workers. Validated when present: work_per_turn finite and > 0 (a 0 means 'no upkeep' while reading like a live dial — say null), meter_decay.per_turn finite and > 0, meter_decay.retain_fraction within 0..=1, and `scaled_by` parsing to a real variant.
_comment_costs: THE SHIPPED COSTS ARE PACING-NEUTRAL, DELIBERATELY (docs/plan_unit_costed_work.md section 3): each is today's 25 turns times the crew that made '25 turns' true, so the inversion ships without a retune and any pacing change in a later slice is visibly an intended one. plant:tended 50 = 25 turns x crew_needed 2; plant:field 75 = 25 x 3. THE TWO ANIMAL RUNGS HAVE NO CREW, SO THEIR COSTS ARE A REFERENCE-CREW CHOICE RATHER THAN A DERIVATION: 2 for `pastoral` (it makes the same claim rung 2 makes on plants — you manage the wild source in place) and 3 for `pen`. A herd's actual crew is `herders_needed`, so real animal pacing now moves in both directions with herd size — the animal rungs were crew-BLIND before (a Tame took 25 turns whether two hands or twenty worked the herd) and a crew-blind build is exactly what this model removes. THE SPREAD ITSELF — a Sow and a Corral costing MORE than a Cultivate, and rung 4 (Farm) being born at ~300 — is a later config-only slice.
_comment_grace: THE NEGLECT GRACE, per rung and deliberately so: a weeded patch reverts in a season, a fence stands for years. The two webs are not even monotone in the same direction — on plants the NEWEST rung is the most fragile (a standing crop wants hands every turn; the cleared, stumped ground under it keeps its clearing longer), while on animals the HIGHEST rung is the most forgiving (the fence does the holding, so the keeper can be away). All four are PLAYTEST ANCHORS, and all four are `upkeep.grace_turns` — the ONE trigger left, consecutive turns of unmet keeping. `build.grace_turns` (the un-worked-build trigger) is `null` on every rung, so a reader chasing this note into a `build` block finds nothing and a reader of that field gets a constant zero. Validated `< work_cost / reference_output`, where the reference output is one worker at the food peak: a grace that outlasts its own build makes walking away free.
_comment_behavior: Config over CODED PRIMITIVES (§5): bounded enums the engine knows how to run. `movement`: fixed | roam | drift_to_owner (the proximity spine far -> near -> fixed; a drifting herd biases each roam step toward its owner's nearest band, composing with — never replacing — the graze-aware roam's barren-avoidance and fertility preference). **`movement` IS READ** by fauna::advance_herds (slice 3b — the first primitive the engine applies), and it is now the ONLY member. RETIRED: `feeding` (photosynthesis | forage | self_graze) and `harvest` (worker_take | worker_tend | passive). Both were declared on every rung, parsed and variant-validated, and read by NOTHING. They were deleted rather than left standing because a declared, validated key reads like a live lever — `harvest` sits exactly where someone debugging the animal draw looks for the answer, and cost an hour of a husbandry investigation before its lack of consumers surfaced. That `movement` also sat dead until slice 3b used it is not a counter-argument: `movement` waiting was free because nothing was looking to it to explain a behaviour. What a rung feeds on and how its take comes off live in the systems that resolve them (fauna::advance_herds, fauna::pen_yield_biomass, forage::field_harvest_biomass). DO NOT RE-ADD EITHER KEY UNTIL A SYSTEM READS IT.
_comment_knowledge: THE PACE OF THE LADDER, AND A LESSON COSTS PRACTICE (docs/plan_unit_costed_work.md sections 2 and 4). `learn_rate` is what ONE TURN of practice is worth in PRACTICE UNITS, charged ONCE PER SOURCE PER TURN a crew works a rung that teaches; `lesson_costs` is what each knowledge costs in those units, keyed by the knowledge name. At learn_rate 1.0 a cost of 20 reads itself: TWENTY WORKED TURNS AT THE FOOD PEAK. TWO CURRENCIES, DELIBERATELY, AND NAMING THEM APART IS WHAT STOPS ANYONE ADDING THEM: a build's `work_cost` is earned by a WORKER-TURN and scales with hands (that is what the build inversion is for); a lesson is earned by a TURN THE SOURCE IS WORKED and MUST NOT scale with hands. Knowledge is faction-level and credited once per source per turn, so a per-worker rate would let a faction learn ten times faster by piling hands onto one patch - the no-cap decision without the opportunity-cost brake that justifies it, since a second lesson costs nothing extra. YOU LEARN BY WATCHING THE PRACTICE, NOT BY COUNTING THE HANDS DOING IT. Both currencies ARE scaled by the FLOOR (docs/plan_harvest_floor.md section 3): intensification::learn_multiplier multiplies the practice by floor / MSY_BIOMASS_FRACTION, so a crew that leaves more standing learns faster in proportion, the food peak 0.5 is exactly x1.0 (which is why the numbers below did not need retuning), stripping the source to 0 learns nothing, and a crew with NOTHING STANDING ABOVE ITS FLOOR learns nothing either. That last gate is the escapement room (max(0, B - floor*K)) read in BIOMASS, before whole-animal quantisation - deliberately not 'a take happened', because a herd whose room is lighter than one body hands over nothing while the crew tracks and handles it exactly as before, and reading that as 'not working' would pace the whole ladder off body_mass. THE LEDGER STAYS NORMALIZED AND THE COST IS A DIVISOR AT THE SEAM: `completion_threshold` is the ledger bar at which the faction KNOWS a discovery and may pick the verb it gates, DiscoveryProgressLedger clamps to 1.0 and is shared with great discoveries, espionage and the start profiles, so RungDef::knowledge_accrual credits `learn_rate x learn_multiplier / lesson_cost` rather than widening the ledger's unit. 1.0 / 20 -> ~20 turns per lesson, which reproduces the retired `progress_per_turn` of 0.05 EXACTLY - the inversion ships pacing-neutral. ALL EIGHT COSTS ARE 20 TODAY; the spread (rung-3's seed_selection and penning dearer, foddering dearer again) is a later config-only slice. EVERY LESSON THE SIM CAN TEACH MUST BE PRICED HERE - validate rejects a ladder missing an entry for any rung's `earns_knowledge` or any craft, because a defaulted cost would pace the lesson off a number nobody chose. The two ladder dials MOVED here from the two identical per-web copies (labor_config's `forage.cultivation` and fauna_config's `husbandry`) once the earn path became one rung-driven seam: a number that paces BOTH webs belongs to the ladder, exactly like the build dials. PLAYTEST DIALS - this is the lever that sets how long the whole wild->pen climb takes.
_comment_knowledge_crafting: AND THE PACE OF THE CRAFTS (docs/plan_crafting_and_materials.md section 5). `craft_lesson_per_item` is what ONE ITEM FINISHED AT A BENCH is worth in PRACTICE UNITS, so `lesson_costs[craft] / this` is a craft's length IN ITEMS: 20 / 4.0 -> 5 items. IT IS A SIBLING OF learn_rate RATHER THAN A READING OF IT, BECAUSE THE QUANTUM DIFFERS - a ladder lesson is charged per TURN WORKED and scaled by the crew's floor, a craft lesson per ITEM COMPLETED, on the SAME quantum as the bench tool's wear so the thing that consumes the tool and the thing that teaches the craft cannot drift. There is no floor to scale it by and no turn to charge it on. IT MOVED WITH THE CURRENCY rather than being left alone: it was `lesson_per_crafted_item` 0.2, a fraction of the normalized threshold, and leaving it that way while its sibling became a COST is precisely the drift the slice-4 consolidation existed to prevent - 4.0 against a cost of 20 is the same 5 items. IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN recipes.json so that every knowledge pace in the game is tuned in ONE file, which is the whole reason the two ladder dials moved here in slice 4. 5 ITEMS IS SET AGAINST THE LADDER'S ~20 TURNS: against the shipped ~17-worker band a kit item costs roughly 4-10 turns of banked material, so a craft is learned in ~25-40 turns of deliberate work - the same order as one rung of the ladder, and the tool it unlocks is then a further ~28-turn investment. THE CRAFTS PACE THEMSELVES OFF THE LAND, which is the point: a gathering band learns Weaving fast (fibre is everywhere - reeds pay 0.02/biomass and a cotton field 0.07), and NOBODY learns Bone-working fast (bone is the scarcest yield on the roster at 0.0012-0.003/biomass). No per-craft dial says so - the three craft costs below are all 20, like every ladder lesson. PLAYTEST DIAL.
_comment_route_traffic: HOW FAST TRAFFIC WEARS A ROAD IN - the route branch's build pace, in the same work units build.work_cost is quoted in. IT IS THE LINK, NOT THE TONNAGE: a live journey banks this much on EACH TILE IT CROSSES per turn, whatever it happened to carry. balance_supply_networks drops sub-min_transfer moves, so a BALANCED network ships nothing - a mass-driven rate would leave two camps who have shared a larder for thirty turns with no path at all, which is exactly the case issue #532 says must not be the one that produces no trail. PER TILE IS NOW LITERAL, and that is the per-tile model's doing: the stored-path model banked rate x path-length onto ONE object, so a 2-tile link put 0.7 a turn into a single road and reached the trail rung's 40 in about 57 turns. Each tile now banks 0.35 of its own, so the same neighbours wear each of their two tiles in over about 114 turns - a long haul wears MANY tiles a little rather than one object a lot, which is what makes 'one band keeps half the tiles and another the other half' a state traffic can actually produce. The model change is deliberately left visible rather than hidden behind a compensating edit. PLAYTEST DIAL, section 4.14 owns the number.
_comment_route_disuse: AND HOW A FREE ROAD IS LOST - the disuse trigger, the free floor's own counterpart to the built rungs' unpaid-keeping trigger (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13a rule 3). A game trail and a trail cost NOTHING to hold, so they cannot be SHORT and the shortfall path can never reach them: what takes them back is the thing that made them, which is traffic. So a road inside the free floor's span that carries no traffic forgives `disuse_grace_turns` consecutive idle turns and then loses `disuse_loss_per_turn` work units off its position every turn until it is gone and the ledger prunes it. THE TWO TRIGGERS DO NOT OVERLAP: this one applies only while the position sits inside the free floor, and the unpaid-keeping decay only above it - a dirt road nobody stands on is lost because nobody PAYS for it, which is rule 3 already. At a grace of 4 and a loss of 1.0 a fully worn trail (40 work) survives a season away and is gone about 44 turns after the last traffic, which is roughly the 57 turns of unbroken neighbourhood it took to wear in - losing a road is meant to be slower than making one. PLAYTEST DIALS, section 4.14 owns both numbers.
_comment_route_range: DISTANCE IS A COST, NEVER A WALL (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13b). There is NO work-range rule on roads - Ray: 'already forage and hunting have different work ranges, expeditions are even farther. I don't think it makes sense to restrict it.' A fourth arbitrary radius would say nothing. What bounds a distant road is that it is dearer to hold and slower to build: within `base_tiles` of the band that took it on, a road costs exactly what the rung says; outside it, BOTH the build pile and the standing upkeep are multiplied by `remote_cost_multiplier`. A THRESHOLD, NOT A CURVE - simpler to tune, and what Ray asked for. *** READ THE RANGE THROUGH routes::road_keeping_range, NEVER FROM THIS FIELD. *** Ray: 'make it a function that can expand over time, don't just create a hardcoded constant. You can have a configuration item for the base range, but still make a function accessor for it so we can calculate it later.' This block is the BASE; the seam is the answer, so the day the range grows with knowledge or a central authority (issue #598) one function body changes and no call site moves. The distance is measured from the keeper band to the road tile AT THE MOMENT THE VERB IS ISSUED and held for the whole job, which is ForagePatch::field_cost_multiplier's discipline: a live reading would move the rung boundaries under a half-built road every time the band took a step. Re-issuing grade/pave re-prices it, which is also how a keeperless road is adopted. PLAYTEST DIALS, section 4.14 owns both numbers.

rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: LIVE (slice 4): working a WILD patch teaches the faction Cultivation (CULTIVATION_DISCOVERY_ID 2003). The earn path reads THIS FIELD — `RungDef::knowledge_accrual`, driven off the rung the patch stands on. The health gate is GONE (docs/plan_harvest_floor.md section 3.2): what remains is 'something stands above the crew's floor' and the floor itself, which sets the RATE.
rungs._comment_site_requirement: THE PLANT BRANCH'S SCARCITY, and it starts at rung 1 because gathering itself is the scarce thing. `requires_gathering_site` means the tile must be a curated FoodSiteRegistry entry — the 130-134 sites worldgen lays down as a share of land, spatially quota'd with minimum spacing and biased toward fresh water — NOT merely a tile carrying a FoodModuleTag, which ~every land tile does and which would make the rule vacuous. So a band cannot gather just anywhere: which site it can reach is the early game's real decision, and the move/stay/fork choice the whole design rests on. It sits on rung 1 rather than being an unwritten property of the Forage verb so that rungs 2-4 inherit or drop it BY CONFIG. No fertility floor and no water rule: a site is workable by definition, which is what being a site means.

rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: SLICE 4, and IT IS A CONFIG EDIT exactly as promised. Working a TENDED patch teaches Seed Selection (2005), at a pace the assignment's floor sets — §4: you learn to select seed by FARMING, not by gathering wild stands. Note the rule is about the RUNG, not the verb: a Sustain harvest of a tended patch teaches it too (the patch is tended; tending it IS the practice). Its consumer — the `Field`/`Sow` rung this gates — is slice 5: earned now, spent later.
rungs._comment_site_requirement: Rung 2 asks exactly what rung 1 asks and nothing more — Cultivate IMPROVES THE OUTPUT of ground you already gather, so it can only stand where gathering can. Stated explicitly rather than left null: an inherited-by-silence rule is one nobody can find, and rung 4 dropping the site term has to read as a deliberate difference from the rungs below it.
rungs._comment_build: work_cost 50 = FIFTY WORKER-TURNS, which was today's 25 turns at the crew of 2 this rung used to declare — the pacing-neutral cost (see _comment_costs at the top of this file). At 1 builder it is 50 turns; at 4 it is 13, and there is no cap beyond the band's own pool. There is no dip here any more: the player states the build's crew on the verb, so a crew preparing this patch costs exactly the hands it names (see the top-of-file note on the retired yield_fraction_while_building). grace_turns is NULL because THIS RUNG COUNTS NO UNWORKED-BUILD TURNS AT ALL: its neglect trigger is the UPKEEP SHORTFALL below, so its grace lives there and a second number here would be a dial nothing reads.
rungs._comment_upkeep: THE DEMAND MOVED, THE ROT DID NOT. work_per_turn 2 is a whole number a player can staff exactly — two hands hold a tended patch — where it used to be 0.5, an inversion artefact (0.01 x this rung's 50-unit cost) that was ALSO the rot rate, because shortfall WAS the decay. meter_decay.per_turn 0.5 is that same artefact kept as what it actually described: a WHOLLY unmaintained patch still loses 0.5 work units a turn, exactly what it always lost, so this retune is provably pacing-neutral on the decay axis and only the price of HOLDING it changed. A patch staffed at one of its two hands is half short and rots at 0.25. retain_fraction IS GONE (see the top-of-file note): with the payout interpolating on the source's one position, a bleeding tended patch does not lose its rung on the first turn and does not hold it at a bar either — it pays a fading share of a tended patch as the position falls from 50 back toward 0, and stops being `tended` the instant it drops below 50. The 2 grace turns and the 0.5 rot rate are what set HOW FAST it fades; re-earning the rung costs exactly the work that rotted, as it always did. scaled_by source_load, and 2 IS QUOTED PER TENDER-LOAD. One tile is exactly what the load measures: a tile's own K over forage.cultivation.capacity_per_tender (195, the reference tile AlluvialPlain's own K), so the reference tile still owes exactly 2 and the rate did not move. Thin ground owes less (PrairieSteppe K 70 -> 0.718) and rich ground more (RiverDelta K 210 -> 2.154) — holding a patch now costs what the size of the place costs. The measure reads the TILE's K and never the patch's carrying_capacity, which has already been multiplied by field_capacity_gain on the very position this demand interpolates on. grace_turns 2 is this rung's own former build grace, moved onto the upkeep's trigger unchanged: cleared, weeded ground keeps its clearing a couple of turns after the crew stops — volunteers close in within a season, not overnight.

rungs._comment_verb: SLICE 5 — the plant twin of `corral`: `sow` PLACES a food source where you want it. Gated on Seed Selection, which the tended rung has been teaching since slice 4 (earned then, spent now — the pacing model working as designed). `Sow` is only legal on WATERED GROUND YOUR PEOPLE ALREADY GATHER (see `_comment_site_requirement`); it CANNOT open rock/ice/desert, or any tile nobody works — making unfamiliar ground farmable is rung 4 (Worked Land), a future arc. So rung 3 pulls you toward the good country you already hold, which IS the sedentarization pull.
rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: Null: practising the field would teach `irrigation`/`rotation` (rung 4 — Worked Land, §2a), a parked follow-on. Exactly where the animal ladder's `pen` rung stands with `selective_breeding`. The engine already reads this field, so adding that rung is a config edit plus one id.
rungs._comment_requires_rung: `requires_rung` states WHERE THIS RUNG SITS ON THE LADDER (directly above `tended`) — it is not a per-source precondition, and no code reads it as one (see RungDef::requires_rung). The per-source rule is each verb's own gate, and it is where the two webs still differ (§2): `corral` demands a herd you already tamed, while `sow` demands no prior PATCH — a gathering site that spawned no forage patch can be sown into a genuinely new source. WHAT THIS COMMENT USED TO SAY — `sow` demands nothing of the tile at all, seed travels — WAS REVERSED BY THE GATHERING-SITE ARC and now belongs to rung 4; the tile rule lives in `_comment_site_requirement` two keys below, which is the authority. Do not read the two as agreeing that any hospitable tile is sowable.
rungs._comment_ceiling_required: Null — the husbandry ceiling is a per-SPECIES gate on the animal branch (`Herd::can_pen`). A plant has no species, so there is no species ceiling here; the LAND is what this rung is choosy about, and that is `site_requirement` below — the plant twin of the same idea.
rungs._comment_site_requirement: Rung 3 is: I know how to take seed from a plant and put it somewhere else — but I do NOT know fertilization or water-carrying, so I must sow ground my people already gather, and it must be near fresh water. `requires_fresh_water` demands a river along one of the hex's sides, fresh-water ground, or a lake/channel/marsh next door (a SALT coast does not count — you do not plant a field in the sea spray). THE GATHERING-SITE RULE IS INHERITED FROM RUNGS 1-2 AND IS WHERE THE SCARCITY NOW LIVES: sites are already few and already the thing a band organises itself around, so rung 3 narrows that set by water rather than starting a second scarcity of its own. `min_forage_capacity` is therefore 0 here — it was 195 (the river-deposit class: RiverDelta 210, Floodplain 205, AlluvialPlain 195) while this rung had no site rule, and stacking both demanded a curated site that ALSO landed on one of three biomes AND had water, which is scarcity three times over on a set the marker list had already made small. It stays a live dial for RUNG 4, which is the rung that actually needs it. PLAYTEST DIAL: drop the water rule to make farmland commoner. RUNG 4 (Farm) IS THIS RECORD WITH `requires_gathering_site: false` AND A FERTILITY FLOOR PUT BACK — that is the whole of what it unlocks.
rungs._comment_build: PLAYTEST DIALS. work_cost 75 = SEVENTY-FIVE WORKER-TURNS, i.e. today's 25 turns at this rung's reference crew of 3 — see _comment_costs at the top of this file. Sowing PLACES a source rather than tidying one, so it is the heavier job, and the Field it buys wants ~10 gatherers anyway; at 2 workers a Sow takes ~38 turns, at 1 it takes 75. Note what a band-level builders pool means on BARE ground: nothing is standing there for anyone to gather, so a bare-ground sow is pure investment — every hand on the `builders` role is a hand eating out of the larder. grace_turns is NULL for the reason the tended rung's is: this rung's neglect trigger is the UPKEEP SHORTFALL below.
rungs._comment_upkeep: THE SAME SPLIT, ONE RUNG UP. work_per_turn 4 is the whole-number demand — a standing crop wants four hands where tended ground wants two, which is the first time the ladder has said a Field is DEARER TO HOLD than the ground beneath it rather than merely dearer to build. meter_decay.per_turn 0.75 is the retired inversion artefact (0.01 x this rung's 75-unit cost) kept unchanged, so a wholly unmaintained field still loses 0.75 a turn and lapses over the same ~100 turns it always did. retain_fraction IS GONE (see the top-of-file note): a Field's payout fades continuously as the position falls from 125 back toward 50, so there is no bar to hold and no cliff for one to guard against. grace_turns 1 and the 0.75 rot rate are what set how fast it fades — and because the position eats from the TOP, the tended ground underneath is untouched until the Field is wholly gone. grace_turns 1: a standing crop is the most perishable thing on the ladder and wants hands every turn — one missed turn is forgiven, two is not. That it is SHORTER than the tended rung's is the point, and it is the same claim the newest-first unwind order makes: the newest improvement is the most fragile. scaled_by source_load, and 4 IS QUOTED PER TENDER-LOAD, exactly as the rung below it is — the same tile's K over the same capacity_per_tender, so the step from 2 to 4 is the RUNG getting dearer and nothing else. CLIMBING TO FIELD DOES NOT COMPOUND THE CAPACITY GAIN: the load is the TILE's K, so field_capacity_gain (2.53) is the payout for the crop standing there and never a multiplier on the bill. Reading the patch's own boosted carrying_capacity instead would land a Field near 10x a tended patch — 2.53 on top of the 2 -> 4 the rate already states — which is a cost nobody chose.
rungs._comment_behavior: A field is a place that photosynthesises and is harvested by its tenders without being drawn down — the same primitives the tended patch recombines. Rung 3 of the plant ladder changes WHERE the source is, not how it behaves; `movement: fixed` is exactly the point (`Sow` fixes the source at a tile of YOUR choosing rather than the one the wild put it on).

rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: LIVE (slice 4), the animal mirror: working a WILD herd teaches the faction Herding (HERDING_DISCOVERY_ID 2004) — §4's "you learn herding by managing wild herds". Read through `RungDef::knowledge_accrual` off the rung the herd stands on. The health gate is GONE (docs/plan_harvest_floor.md section 3.2): what remains is 'something stands above the crew's floor' — the escapement room in biomass, NOT 'an animal was brought down', which is a quantisation fact — and the floor itself, which sets the RATE.

rungs._comment_verb: The `tame` verb — the animal twin of `cultivate`. Taming is an EXPLICIT, gated investment, no longer a hidden side effect of a Sustain hunt (the §4.1 conflation, fixed): Sustain now only TEACHES the faction Herding, and `tame` is what fills this herd's meter. The `domesticate` early-claim is gone (it existed to skip the investment — the same reason the plant side removed its own).
rungs._comment_unlock_knowledge: §4.3, COMPLETE as of slice 4: Herding gates rung 2 (`tame`) and NOTHING ELSE — the `animal:pen` rung moved onto its own `penning` knowledge, so there is now exactly ONE knowledge per transition.
rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: SLICE 4, a config edit: working a PASTORAL (tamed) herd teaches Penning (2006) — §4's "...penning by managing tamed ones", which is the heart of the arc. Again the rule keys off the RUNG, not the verb: a Sustain hunt of a tamed herd teaches Penning, while the same Sustain hunt of a wild one teaches Herding. PACING CONSEQUENCE (intended): a pen now needs Sustain-hunt-wild -> Herding -> Tame -> work the pastoral herd -> Penning -> Corral, materially longer than the old "Herding unlocks Corral". Each rung is paced by practising the one below.
rungs._comment_ceiling_required: Grazing 2d-delta: a species may only be tamed if its `husbandry_ceiling` reaches `pastoral` (Herd::can_domesticate).
rungs._comment_upkeep: THE PACING-NEUTRAL INVERSION OF `herders_needed`, NOT A CHOSEN VALUE. A managed herd used to declare its keeper demand as a HEAD COUNT — ceil((biomass / body_mass) / animals_per_herder) — and that count is now a WORK RATE like every other standing cost: work_per_turn 1.0 x scaled_by source_load, where the load is the herd's own `head count / animals_per_herder` (fauna::herd_keeper_loads). Since one worker-turn is PER_WORKER_OUTPUT = 1.0, ceil(demand) IS the old ceil, so EVERY SPECIES ASKS FOR EXACTLY THE KEEPERS IT ASKED FOR BEFORE — a shepherd still minds 200 fowl and a cowherd still minds 12 aurochs. THE PER-SPECIES RATIO STAYS IN fauna_config.json's animals_per_herder, which is where it belongs: the species owns the ratio, the rung owns the rate, exactly as taming_cost_multiplier and work_cost divide the taming job. grace_turns 2 is this rung's own former build grace, moved onto the upkeep's trigger unchanged: a tamed herd with no fence stays near its people out of habit for a turn or two, then drifts.
rungs._comment_build: work_cost 50 = FIFTY WORKER-TURNS, times the species' `taming_cost_multiplier` (fauna_config.json — a Steppe Runner is FIVE TIMES THE WORK, 250 units, where the retired `taming_rate` said the crew was five times worse at the job). THE 50 IS A REFERENCE-CREW CHOICE, NOT A DERIVATION: this rung declares no crew, so there was no crew to multiply today's 25 turns by, and 2 is what rung 2 of the plant web wants for the same claim (you manage the wild source in place). A herd's real crew is `herders_needed`, so a Tame now takes 25 turns at 2 keepers, 5 at 10 and 50 at 1 — the rung was crew-BLIND before, and a crew-blind build is exactly what the work model removes. decay_fraction_per_turn is NULL and that is a DELETION, not a retune: the neglect-escape arc made `domestication_progress` monotone-up, so the 0.01 that sat here was read by NOTHING (RungDef::build_decay has two production call sites, both on the plant branch) and documented a tameness-bleed the sim does not have. grace_turns 2: a tamed herd with no fence stays near its people out of habit for a turn or two, then drifts — the same number as the plant rung 2, because both rungs make the same claim (you manage the wild source in place). PLAYTEST DIALS.
rungs._comment_behavior: Slice 3b, the thesis in action — THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IS THIS DIFF. `harvest` was `passive` (a tamed herd paid its owner with no workers at all); §3 retires that: EVERY rung is worker-driven, so a pastoral herd is now `worker_take` like a wild one — it yields only through a normal Hunt assignment. The payoff is not zero workers, it is YIELD PER WORKER: `herd_ecology` already gives a tamed herd the pastoral r (wild x `pastoral_gain` 1.5), so the same workers take ~1.5x the sustainable food. `movement` was `roam`; it is now `drift_to_owner` — the proximity spine's middle rung (wild roams its full range, tamed drifts to the camp, penned is fixed at the fence), which is also less chasing and so more effective yield.

rungs._comment_unlock_knowledge: THE §4.3 RESHUFFLE (slice 4): `herding` -> `penning`. Rung 3 is gated on the knowledge rung 2 TEACHES, so you cannot pen a herd until you have kept tamed ones. Herding now gates `tame` alone. The `extend_pen` command rides this same rung record, so a fence ring is gated on Penning too — a ring is the same fencing labor at the same price, and it must never drift from the initial build.
rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: FLORA ROSTER F3 (docs/plan_flora_roster.md §5.2), a config edit: working a PENNED herd teaches Foddering (FODDERING_DISCOVERY_ID 2007) — 'you learn to hay a herd by keeping one'. Foddering is NOT a new rung with a verb; it only unlocks a pen's ability to draw the band's FODDER store as delivered graze-flow (the feed term + the K_pen fodder term). Read through `RungDef::knowledge_accrual` off the rung the herd stands on, exactly like every other earned knowledge. A rung-3 source is TENDED rather than drawn from, so its keeper learns at the ladder's stated pace whatever floor the assignment names — the floor axis has collapsed there (intensification::MANAGED_SOURCE_FLOOR). (`selective_breeding`, rung 4's lesson, is still parked — one earn slot per rung, and F3 spends this one.)
rungs._comment_ceiling_required: Grazing 2d-delta: only a `pen`-ceiling species may be fenced (Herd::can_pen).
rungs._comment_upkeep: THE SAME RATE, A LONGER GRACE — and the difference is the fence. work_per_turn 1.0 x source_load is identical to the pastoral rung's, because a penned animal is not less work to mind than an unfenced one and moving that number would break the pacing-neutrality this slice is built on. WHAT THE FENCE BUYS IS TIME: grace_turns 6 against pastoral's 2, this rung's own former build grace moved across unchanged — the turns-side statement of the same claim fauna_config's pen_escape_fraction (0.10) < pastoral_escape_fraction (0.25) already makes about the RATE animals leave at. Do not flatten the two: a pen that forgave neglect no longer than open range would make the fence worth nothing but its capacity.
rungs._comment_upkeep_materials: THE MATERIAL HALF OF HOLDING THE RUNG (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.7, 4.9 item 12), and hurdles are the reference implementation because a fence panel is a thing you build IN and leave BEHIND — it is spent, and no number of hands replaces it. 0.05 hurdles per keeper-load per turn: a fence frays, and mending it swallows panels at a fifth of the rate one goes into raising it. IT READS THE SAME `scaled_by` THE WORK TERM READS — one rule, two currencies — so a pen holding twice the herd mends twice the fence exactly as it takes twice the hands. AND IT IS NOT FEED: hay is what the animals EAT and it is settled by `settle_pen_hay` in fodder units against the herd's appetite; this is what the STRUCTURE costs to stand, and it would be owed by an empty pen just the same. A SHORTFALL OF EITHER KIND TRIPS THE SAME grace_turns AND THE SAME NEGLECT COUNTER: the amounts stay separate so a full store cannot paper over missing hands, and the fraction that drives the decay is the WORST of the two. NOTHING BELOW THIS RUNG NAMES A MATERIAL, and the monotonicity rule is per id — a rung may not swallow LESS of a good than the rung under it, because the demand interpolates as a delta. OPENING VALUES CHOSEN FOR SHAPE, NOT BALANCE — playtest dials, and the tuning spread of section 4.14 is what moves them.
rungs._comment_build_materials: THE MATERIAL HALF OF RAISING THE RUNG. 6 hurdles per pen, DRAWN AS THE METER CLIMBS rather than on completion (section 2.7): a fence a third raised has swallowed two of them, and DECAY REFUNDS NOTHING — panels go into the ground and do not come back out when the position falls, which is what makes neglect self-limiting rather than a store bleeding for ever. A SHORT STORE STALLS THE BUILD PROPORTIONALLY AND NEVER REFUSES IT: the coverage fraction scales both the work banked and the materials drawn, and the unbanked work is WASTED, which is section 2.5's stated rule for an indivisible supplier. The pile takes NO per-species multiplier, exactly as work_cost does not on this rung — a fence is a fence. AN EXTENSION RING DRAWS THIS SAME PILE, off this same record: widening a pen is a pen build, so a ring costs 6 hurdles exactly as the work_cost beside it charges a ring the full 75 work units, and the two can no more drift than the work halves can. The ring lays one leg (systems::labor::head_ring_leg) and goes through the SAME build_material_wants every rung leg goes through, at the source row's own SourcePriority in the SAME settle_material_upkeep pass - so a short store stalls a widening fence in proportion and a dry one blocks it with BuildGate::Materials, and a ring and a fresh pen draw the same panels for the same work banked. OPENING VALUES CHOSEN FOR SHAPE, NOT BALANCE — playtest dials, section 4.14.
rungs._comment_build: work_cost 75 = SEVENTY-FIVE WORKER-TURNS per pen / per extension ring, a REFERENCE-CREW choice of 3 against today's 25 turns for the reason the `pastoral` rung's note gives (this rung declares no crew either). Penning is a flat cost for every species — a fence is a fence — so it takes no per-species multiplier; only TAMING varies. decay_fraction_per_turn is NULL rather than the old 0.0: pen construction does not bleed, and `null` says so where a `0` read like a live dial that happened to be parked. grace_turns 6: the fence does the holding, so an abandoned pen keeps its flock far longer than an unfenced pastoral herd keeps its — the turns-side statement of the same claim `pen_escape_fraction < pastoral_escape_fraction` already makes about the rate. PLAYTEST DIALS.
rungs._comment_partial_credit: THE ONE RUNG ON THE SHIPPED LADDER THAT IS ALL-OR-NOTHING, and it is a RUNG PROPERTY rather than a pen special case — nothing in the code asks 'is this the pen rung'. A pen is a FENCE AT A TILE, and half a fence is not a fence: until it is up the animals are on the open range, drifting with their people, leaking at the OPEN-RANGE rate (fauna_config's pastoral_escape_fraction 0.25, not the pen's 0.10) and hunted out of a wild stock rather than collected off a fenced footprint. So there is no fraction of a pen to pay for and no fraction of one to charge for: a source part-way up this rung pays and costs EXACTLY the pastoral rung under it, and steps to the pen's own numbers the turn the meter fills. Every other rung is absent from this key and therefore `continuous`, which is the default because SMOOTHING IS WHAT THE ARC IS FOR — a rung that is all-or-nothing has to be argued for here, in the config, and cannot be fallen into by silence. The test for a future rung is whether the thing it buys EXISTS in part: cleared ground is partly cleared, a standing crop is partly sown, a herd is partly gentled — a fence is not partly a fence.

rungs._comment_rung: THE ROUTE BRANCH'S FLOOR, and it is a real thing rather than the absence of one: a GAME TRAIL is what traffic leaves behind before anybody decides to make a road (issue #215 - 'the first roads are the ones the animals made'). It costs nothing to reach and it buys nothing, exactly as plant:wild and animal:wild do, so a route at position 0 already HOLDS it. build and upkeep are both null: NOBODY MAINTAINS A GAME TRAIL, which is the whole of what makes this rung free - and it is also why it does not light its tiles (routes.rs Route::grants_sight reads the PAID BILL, and this rung has none).
rungs._comment_verb: THE FREE FLOOR IS TWO RUNGS AND TRAFFIC STOPS AT THE TOP OF IT (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13a). A game trail and a trail are FORMED BY USE: traffic wears them in, there is no command to name the job and no crew to staff it, and NEITHER COSTS ANYTHING TO HOLD - exactly the shape plant:wild and animal:wild already have. 13a billed the trail, so two camps that shared a larder wore one in by themselves and their band acquired a standing labour bill it never opted into; and moving that line without also CAPPING the traffic at the top of the free floor would only relocate the fault one rung up, because traffic would go on wearing a DIRT ROAD in for free and hand the player its bill anyway. The cap is routes::traffic_ceiling. THE TWO BUILT RUNGS DECLARE THEIR VERBS - `grade` and `pave`, TILE commands in cultivate/sow's own grammar (`grade <faction> <band> <x> <y>`), because a road is a PER-TILE improvement and not a path object. Issuing one names the ordering band as that tile's KEEPER, exactly as `cultivate` names a patch's owner, and one tile has exactly ONE keeper.
rungs._comment_earns_knowledge: THE FLOOR TEACHES NOTHING, and the lesson it used to teach was deleted rather than moved. It earned `trailcraft`, which gated `trail` - A LESSON FOR SOMETHING YOU CANNOT FAIL TO DO. You wear a path by walking it; there is no knowing-how involved and no way to be refused, so the gate could only ever be open by the time it mattered. `trailcraft` is gone from lesson_costs and from start_profile_knowledge_tags.json, and DISCOVERY ID 2011 IS RETIRED - not reused, and 2012/2013 are not renumbered onto it, because a gap is safer than a renumber. The surviving chain is trail -> roadbuilding -> dirt road -> paving -> paved road, and every lesson in it gates something a player actually decides.
rungs._comment_site_requirement: NULL ON EVERY ROUTE RUNG, and that is the honest answer rather than a gap. site_requirement asks what the LAND UNDER THIS TILE must be, and a road asks nothing of it - there is no ground a road refuses to cross. What a road asks of the land is PRICED, not gated: it is the upkeep's scaled_by term, the tile's own infrastructure_cost. DO NOT INVENT a route_requirement sibling to fill this hole; a rung asking nothing of its site is what every animal rung already ships.
rungs._comment_route_payoff: THE FLOOR BUYS NOTHING, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. Both terms are their own neutral: a trail the animals made holds no pooling link open beyond the free reach, and takes nothing off the friction. These are LIVE READINGS, not parked dials - 'this rung is worth nothing' is precisely what the branch's floor means, the same way min_forage_capacity 0 is a live dial on the plant rungs.

rungs._comment_rung: A TRAIL - THE FREE FLOOR'S SECOND STOREY, and NOT the first rung anyone pays for (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13a). work_cost 40 is what the traffic between two neighbouring camps banks over a few dozen turns rather than what a crew builds in an afternoon: TRAFFIC IS THE CREW here, so the figure is a duration in traffic, not in worker-turns off a pool - and it is the TOP OF WHAT TRAFFIC MAY BANK, because traffic that kept climbing would wear a dirt road in for free and hand the player its bill anyway. `upkeep` IS NULL, and that is this slice's correction: a trail carried 0.20 per unit of span, so two camps that shared a larder wore a trail into existence by themselves and their band acquired a standing labour bill it never opted into - reported from play as a 7-worker nomadic band showing Roadwork with no road it had chosen. Nothing else in the game does that: a wild patch and a wild herd sit at their free floor for ever until the player issues cultivate / tame and staffs the builders. A rung that costs nothing to hold cannot be SHORT, so what takes a trail back is DISUSE rather than shortfall - see _comment_route_disuse at the head of this file. It still EARNS `roadbuilding`, because a trail carrying traffic is the practice, and it still buys its payoff: the floor is free, not worthless.

A DIRT ROAD - THE FIRST RUNG ANYBODY BUILDS AND THE FIRST ANYBODY PAYS FOR (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13a). Traffic banks nothing above the trail beneath it, so this rung is reached only because somebody said so: `grade <faction> <band> <x> <y>` appends an entry to that band's build queue and makes the tile that band's job. `scaled_by` is `source_load`, whose ROUTE reading is the tile's own infrastructure_cost times what distance did to the price (routes::road_upkeep_measure) - the same shape the plant web reads its tile's K in, which is why the `route_span` variant retired into it. The rung where reach starts to matter: holds_link_to_tiles 10 against the shipped reach_tiles of 3, so a road is what lets two camps pool at a distance where they simply cannot today - a CAPABILITY, not a discount, and the reason the top rungs are about distance at all. Dearer to keep than the trail beneath it per unit of span, and more forgiving of neglect (grace 5 against 2), which is the direction the ANIMAL branch runs in: the highest rung is the most forgiving, because the roadbed does the holding. OPENING VALUES CHOSEN FOR SHAPE, NOT BALANCE - playtest dials, and the tuning spread of section 4.14 is what moves them.

A PAVED ROAD - the top of the branch, gated on `paving`, raised by `pave <faction> <band> <x> <y>` on the keeping band's builders pool, and the ONLY route rung that swallows a material. Stone on the pile AND on the rate, which is the material half of section 2.7 applied unchanged: the pile draws in proportion to the work banked, the rate scales with how much of the rung stands, and DECAY REFUNDS NOTHING - the road washes out and the stone is spent. That is what makes neglect self-limiting rather than a store bleeding for ever. THE QUARRYING AND HAULING ARE THE UPKEEP, not a second line beside it (section 2.7 disposes of that explicitly). It reads the same scaled_by the work term reads, so a road through harder country eats proportionally more stone. earns_knowledge is null: this is the top of the branch and there is nothing above it to teach. OPENING VALUES CHOSEN FOR SHAPE, NOT BALANCE - playtest dials, and the tuning spread of section 4.14 is what moves them.
rungs._comment_materials: NO ROUTE RUNG DECLARES A MATERIAL IN 13a, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE MATERIAL DOES NOT EXIST. The design (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.13) has the paved road swallowing STONE on both the pile and the rate - the material half of section 2.7, applied unchanged. It is not declared here because `stone` is not in materials.json: the shipped roster is bone / fibre / grape / hide / hurdles / tea / tobacco / wood, and the ladder's own load-time check rejects a rung naming a material the table does not carry, for exactly the right reason - 'a rung that eats a material nobody defines draws nothing, for ever, with no fault reported anywhere'. ADDING A STONE MATERIAL WITH NO WAY TO OBTAIN ONE WOULD BE WORSE THAN DECLARING NONE: it would ship a rung that can never be held, which is a harder failure than a rung that is cheap to hold. Quarrying is the crafting arc's to add, not this branch's - and section 4.9 item 12's own rule cuts this way too, a mechanism whose only consumer is the next slice is the failure mode. When a stone material lands, this rung takes `build.materials {stone: 30}` and `upkeep.materials {stone: 0.08}` and NOTHING ELSE CHANGES - the engine half already ships.
